title: Fake the network at its edge
prompt:
`loadGroup(groupId, fetchImpl)` requests `https://api.splitwise-lite.test/groups/<id>`, converts the API's JSON (dollars, snake_case) into Splitwise-lite's shape (cents, camelCase), and rejects with `Could not load group <id> (HTTP <status>)` when the response isn't ok. The exact shapes are in the subject's comment.

The starter gives you `jsonResponse(body, status)`, which builds a real `Response`, and an `apiGroup` sample. Pass a `vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(jsonResponse(...))` as `fetchImpl` and add tests until your suite catches four hidden bugs: one **ignores** the HTTP status, one requests the **wrong URL**, one forgets to convert dollars to **cents**, and one reads `paidBy` from the wrong field.
hints: Compare the whole result with `toEqual`; the expected object is spelled out in the subject comment (45.5 dollars is 4550 cents).
For the error path, use `jsonResponse({ error: 'Not found' }, 404)` and assert the message, not just that it rejects: the buggy version rejects too, with a TypeError.
explanation: Because only the transport is faked, every line of `loadGroup` runs in the test. `toHaveBeenCalledWith` on the fetch mock catches the wrong URL, which no assertion on the result could see, since a fake answers any URL. One `toEqual` on the converted group catches both shaping bugs: dollars left as 45.5 and `paidBy` coming back `undefined`. The 404 test is the subtle one: without the `ok` check, the code still rejects, with `Cannot read properties of undefined`, so only matching the message `HTTP 404` proves the status was handled on purpose. This is the same discipline MSW gives you, without the library.

checks.passes: All your tests pass against the real loadGroup
checks.catches-ignores-status: Catches the version that ignores the HTTP status
checks.catches-wrong-url: Catches the version that requests the wrong URL
checks.catches-no-cents: Catches the version that keeps dollars instead of cents
checks.catches-snake-case-leak: Catches the version that reads paidBy from the wrong field
